label: Richard N. Boyd, How to be a Moral Realist…: An ascription of the evaluative property to an act is…
locator: reprint §1.1, pp. 307–308: moral statements and truth
interpretation: Formalized only for an atomic ascription of a property the theory treats as real. It describes a fact rather than expressing approval alone. This minimal descriptive reading does not establish the proponent’s naturalistic identification or a full theory of linguistic meaning.
